assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made a superconducting circuit act as an artificial atom coupled to a single microwave photon in a resonator, with dispersive readout and coherent control. It is the architecture behind essentially all superconducting quantum processors and microwave quantum optics on a chip, so its originality, clarity and lasting impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 proposal (Blais, Huang, Girvin, Schoelkopf) and the first strong-coupling experiments (Wallraff, Schoelkopf and colleagues) define the discovery; the supplied trio of Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf is a natural theory plus two-experiment split. Other contributors to the original proposal and to related early circuit work may be left out, so some credit remains unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by two decades of independent work in many laboratories and now an industrial platform; interpretation is stable. Timing is good, although the 2025 prize already recognised superconducting-circuit quantum effects, so the committee must judge how far this is a distinct discovery.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits needs a clear argument for why cQED is a separate achievement.
Allocation of credit among theorists and experimentalists (Girvin, Huang, Nakamura-type circuit work) is not settled by the supplied names.
My own field and institution (Chalmers, WACQT) are close to this work; I would flag a possible conflict of interest and rely on the evidence rather than personal familiarity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators introduced a new classification of electronic phases by topology and protected edge or surface states. The idea is original, conceptually clear and has changed condensed-matter physics well beyond the original systems.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the Z2 theory and the graphene model; Molenkamp led the HgTe experimental observation of edge transport following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. The supplied names give a defensible trio, but the BHZ theory contribution is missing from the credited names and Zhang's death in 2018 limits who can be honoured.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent experimental confirmation (transport, ARPES in Bi-based materials) and a mature field with an established theory. Recognition is timely and not premature, though the 2016 prize already honoured topological phases of matter.
uncertainties: Whether the 2016 topological-phases prize reduces the room for another topology prize.
Credit for the HgTe proposal and for the three-dimensional topological insulators is split among people not in the credited list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combined the magic-wavelength trapping idea with large ensembles of atoms interrogated at optical frequencies, reaching fractional uncertainties near 1e-18. It underpins redefinition of the second, tests of fundamental constants and relativistic geodesy, so the impact is clear and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and built the first strontium clocks; Ye brought the system to extreme accuracy and coherence. Two laureates fit the supplied credit cleanly. Ye shared the 2005 prize for frequency combs, which is a separate contribution. Others contributed to ion and lattice clocks, but the credited pair is a coherent core.
assessment.maturity: Many independent laboratories have confirmed performance, and the clocks are in international comparisons. Timing is mature, perhaps overdue.
uncertainties: The 2005 prize and the 2012 prize on ion control cover neighbouring techniques, so the novelty relative to those must be argued.
Contributions to the ion clock and lattice-clock developments by others are not captured in the credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire materials as a tunable platform for strongly correlated physics. It is a rare case of theory and experiment closely linked.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the continuum-model prediction of the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group led the 2018 observation of correlated and superconducting states. The three names form a clear theory-plus-experiment configuration. Contributions by Dean, Kim, Yazdani and others on moire materials are not in the list.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups, but the field is only about eight years old and the origin of the superconductivity is still debated. Reasonable timing, yet some risk of being early.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity and nature of the correlated states remain unsettled.
Whether others working on moire heterostructures deserve credit that the three-person limit would exclude.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cirac and Zoller proposed quantum logic with laser-cooled trapped ions and, with others, quantum simulation and quantum-optics schemes for cold atoms. The ion-trap gate proposal was a founding blueprint for quantum computing and has been implemented widely; the ideas shaped the whole quantum-simulation program.
assessment.attribution: The 1995 proposal is clearly theirs and the pair is a natural, compact configuration. Experimental realisation by Wineland, Blatt and others should not be confused with the theory credit. The bundled optical-lattice work (with Jaksch and Bloch) is a separate stream with a different credit pattern.
assessment.maturity: Decades of experimental confirmation, with working quantum processors. Recognition is mature, possibly delayed. Prior prizes (2012) honoured control of single quantum systems rather than this theory.
uncertainties: The compound candidate mixes ion-gate theory and optical-lattice simulation, which may need different credit.
Wineland's 2012 recognition for experimental control may be considered to overlap.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 introduced quantum key distribution with security based on quantum measurement, and is the first practical quantum-information protocol with real-world deployment. It has strong originality and conceptual clarity, and it is a core part of quantum information science.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard authored BB84 and are the decisive contributors. Ekert's 1991 entanglement-based protocol is an independent route linked to Bell tests, and including him would make the configuration of three; whether that is fair is uncertain, so I propose the pair.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally demonstrated for decades and commercialised, with ongoing security-proof and implementation-attack work. The 2022 prize recognised entanglement and Bell tests, so timing is plausible but the practical security side is still evolving.
uncertainties: Whether Ekert should share credit for independent discovery of entanglement-based QKD.
Possible overlap with the 2022 prize and with the teleportation entry (B016), which lists the same three names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube detected a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and identified TXS 0506+056 as a source, opening neutrino astronomy at TeV-PeV energies. It is an experimental milestone, building on the 2002 neutrino prize.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the project; Karle played a central role in the detector and analysis. Collaboration of several hundred people means any two-person credit is a simplification, and the Antarctic detector design builds on the earlier AMANDA programme.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux has been confirmed by other analyses and by KM3NeT and Baikal data, while the individual source identifications are still few. Substantial but still maturing.
uncertainties: Large-collaboration attribution and the role of AMANDA pioneers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Precision mapping of CMB anisotropy and its acoustic peaks fixed the parameters of the standard cosmological model with percent-level accuracy. The importance is very high, although the 2006 prize for COBE and the 2019 prize for physical cosmology already cover related ground.
assessment.attribution: WMAP leaders Bennett, Page and Spergel are a coherent mission-based trio. Sunyaev, Puget and others made foundational theory and Planck or balloon contributions that the three-name limit leaves out. This is a hard allocation.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by Planck, ACT, SPT and balloon experiments, so very mature. Recognition is timely, possibly overdue.
uncertainties: Excluded contributors (Sunyaev, Puget, Planck and balloon teams) make the credit contested.
